classification.analysis: Starmer resigned in late June 2026 after Reform UK overtook Labour in polls, forcing his departure after just two years. Labour collapsed from 33.7% to around 20-24%, while Reform surged from 14.3% to 25%. His 76% dissatisfaction rating marked the lowest ever for a departing PM. Andy Burnham replaced him in late July.

Merz's CDU-SPD coalition trails AfD by six points nationally, having lost over 10 points since the February 2025 election. After months of internal deadlock, the coalition delivered a 34-point reform package in July, but faces critical September state elections where AfD polls near 40% in eastern Germany.

Macron's approval has collapsed to 18%, among the lowest of any democratic leader globally. The National Rally dominates 2027 presidential polling at 34-37%, while Marine Le Pen confirmed her candidacy despite embezzlement convictions. Consumer confidence remains depressed at 89, below the long-term average, reflecting broader economic pessimism amid political paralysis.

Sánchez confronts converging crises: mass wildfires forcing evacuations, Ceuta migration incident with 50,000 crossings, corruption cases affecting his family, and three years of rolled-over budgets amid parliamentary deadlock. Polls show PP-Vox bloc commanding 51% and path to majority, while coalition has shed five points since 2023 election.

Coalition negotiations following March 2026 election produced historic losses for all three governing parties. Frederiksen forming new left-leaning coalition with Green Left and Social Liberals after SVM bloc collapsed from 50% to 40%. Danish People's Party surged from 2.6% to 11% but remains secondary opposition force. Consumer confidence weakening amid political instability.

One Nation surged to overtake Labor in multiple polls after winning their first-ever House seat in the Farrer by-election. Their 'Fire The Liar' fundraiser targeting Albanese raised over $4 million, though Labor maintains a comfortable two-party preferred lead. Consumer confidence remains deeply pessimistic at 83.9, well below the 100 neutrality threshold.

classification.cci_source: Irish Credit Union Consumer Sentiment Index
classification.analysis: Martin's coalition holds power 18 months after winning November 2024 election but has dropped 5.7 points in polling. Ireland assumed EU Council presidency July 1, with Martin addressing European Parliament. April fuel protests over Iran war price spikes pressured government. No far-right threat exists; left-nationalist Sinn Féin leads opposition. Consumer confidence weak but improving year-over-year amid housing crisis.

Jetten's centrist coalition faces mounting pressure five months in, with consumer confidence collapsing from -23 to -46 since February and polling support dropping from 59% at election to 52%. Twelve percent of D66 voters consider defecting over right-leaning policies, though PVV remains contained at 11.7%, down from 16.7%. Majority of voters doubt cabinet will complete term.

Montenegro's minority government faces mounting pressure after polling collapsed from 31% to 25.5%, while Chega surged to 24.4%. The government has relied on far-right support for controversial immigration reforms, drawing union criticism for labour changes. Consumer confidence deteriorated significantly, and Montenegro canceled his summer holiday amid growing challenges including criticism over wildfire and storm responses.

Støre's government faces severe pressure as Progress Party surges to 30.1% in polls, overtaking Labour's 22.3%. The far-right now leads as consumer confidence deteriorates. All parties united in June on defense amid Trump's tariffs on Norway. Coalition support has collapsed since the 2025 election victory.

Takaichi's approval plummeted from 70% to low-40s after prioritizing divisive bills over cost-of-living concerns. Parliament passed all 64 government bills including controversial Osaka secondary capital legislation. She announced temporary food sales tax cut to 1% to appease voters amid weak yen hitting 40-year lows. Far-right Sanseito quintupled seats; Takaichi adopted its anti-foreigner policies.

Estonia's tripartite coalition has cratered to 28% from 54% at the 2023 election, losing ground primarily to conservative Isamaa (26%) and Centre (22%). July polls show Reform recovering slightly to 14%, tied with EKRE. PM Michal signed Ukraine drone pact at NATO Ankara Summit despite domestic weakness. Far-right EKRE stable at 13.5%, not leading opposition.

Kristersson's coalition collapsed from 49.6% bloc support to 25.1%, losing its majority ahead of September 13 elections. After committing in April to bring Sweden Democrats into cabinet with ministerial posts, the government enacted controversial migration deportation laws in July, marking the formal end of the cordon sanitaire around the far-right.

Orpo's coalition with the far-right Finns Party narrowly survived a confidence vote on July 21 following a lobbying scandal over Garden Helsinki arena funding. Coalition support has collapsed from 50% to 40% since the 2023 election, while consumer confidence remains persistently negative. The government continues implementing controversial austerity measures despite growing opposition pressure.

Mitsotakis faces mounting pressure despite maintaining a polling lead. His government is embroiled in an EU farm subsidy fraud scandal involving party lawmakers, while July firebomb attacks on New Democracy politicians killed one person. Consumer confidence has deteriorated and support has fallen 14 points since the 2023 landslide. Early election speculation grows ahead of Greece's 2027 EU presidency.

Stocker's ÖVP-SPÖ-NEOS coalition has collapsed from 56.5% at the 2024 election to just 44% in polls, while FPÖ surged to 37.5%. In mid-July, the Chancellor condemned FPÖ's divisive rhetoric. Consumer confidence remains deeply negative. The coalition barely holds a parliamentary majority at 47% of seats—far-right consolidation accelerating.

De Wever's five-party coalition maintains a solid 57.3% majority despite slipping from election results. Vlaams Belang remains contained at 16% under the cordon sanitaire. Consumer confidence has improved from -11 to -5 but remains negative. Tens of thousands protested austerity reforms in March, while De Wever attacks previous governments' nuclear policy legacy in parliament.

National has slumped to historic low of 28.7% while coalition partner NZ First surged to 11.5%, nearly doubling since 2023. Coalition clings to 61-seat majority ahead of November election. Winston Peters' racist remarks toward Chinese-born MP forced Luxon damage control. Consumer confidence recovering to 99.3 but remains subdued. Coalition weakening as junior populist partner gains leverage.

Meloni's far-right coalition has lost its projected parliamentary majority in polling, falling to 41% from 44% at election. After suffering its first parliamentary defeat on electoral reform in mid-July, the government subsequently won approval for revised legislation. Consumer confidence declined year-over-year despite July uptick. Coalition partners showing internal tensions.

Babiš coalition actively dismantling pro-Ukraine policies; SPD speaker removed Ukrainian flag from parliament. Defense minister publicly contradicted president's Ukraine pledge. Coalition ministers suffer 60%+ disapproval. Government won confidence vote but lost 8-9 points since October election. President-government conflicts intensifying over NATO representation and foreign policy direction.

Trump's approval hits second-term low of 38.2% as Iran war drags into fifth month with ceasefire collapsed. Planning fresh strikes despite diplomatic failures. Consumer confidence declining steadily since late 2021, now at 90.8. Expectations Index below recessionary threshold since February 2025, signaling economic pessimism amid ongoing Middle East conflict.

Magyar's aggressive dismantling of Orbán-era institutions triggered first polling decline (68%, down 5 points) three months into office. Prosecutor general resigned late July under pressure. Despite commanding lead over Fidesz (24%), internal criticism emerging over pace of reform. Consumer confidence surged +15.4 points year-over-year, highest gain globally.

Fico survived a crushing July 4 referendum defeat when only 16% turnout invalidated opposition attempts to strip his lifetime pension and restore anti-corruption agencies. Despite this tactical victory, his coalition has collapsed from 43% to 28% in polls, trailing Progressive Slovakia's 20%. Economic sentiment remains weak at 97.8 with consumer confidence deeply negative at -27.3.

Milei's approval collapsed to 35.5% by July 2026 from 70% at inauguration as corruption scandals eroded his anti-establishment brand. Consumer confidence fell to 40.67 amid 30% public spending cuts. Central bank reform announced July 30 as 2027 election talk intensifies with opposition mobilizing.

Netanyahu faces electoral collapse as coalition polls at 51 seats versus 64 in 2022. ICC arrest warrant, pending criminal trial, and October 7 inquiry loom. Government's judicial overhaul, multi-front war, and settlement expansion have driven international isolation. Despite far-right consolidation, overall bloc hemorrhaging support with opposition commanding 69-seat majority in polls.

Courts invalidated opposition CHP leadership in May, forcing ousted leader Özel to launch new party in July. US imposed 12.5% tariffs on Turkish goods. Consumer confidence rose to 89.8 but remains below pessimism threshold. Erdoğan's approval at 46% trails opposition mayors; AKP polls at 29.7% vs CHP's 34.3%.

Coalition support has fallen from 53.7% to 45.6% since 2023 election, losing parliamentary majority in polls. Confederation doubled to 14.3%. Third Way alliance dissolved, with PSL and Poland 2050 now polling separately at just 3.6% and 1.6%. PiS opposition fragmenting after Morawiecki split. Russian missile incident on July 30 heightens security tensions. Consumer confidence improving but remains negative.

Carney maintains strong polling despite slip from spring peak. Recent infrastructure deal with Alberta and poaching of fifth Conservative MP demonstrate continued momentum. Liberal support remains 5 points below election result but well ahead of opposition. PPC irrelevant at 1%. Government navigating minority parliament while building toward potential majority.

Lee's approval has dropped from 60% at his one-year mark to 46.3% in late July, driven by apartment sale controversy and property tax remarks amid stock market volatility. Consumer confidence remains above 100 but softening. Rising Seoul home prices test his reformist promises as the honeymoon fades.

Sheinbaum's approval surged after attending World Cup final with Trump, reaching 74.3% in late July. She's navigating tensions with US over ICE deaths of Mexican nationals and rejecting DEA claims of cartel-government ties. Consumer confidence has declined from its October 2024 peak but economic rebound projected for second half of year.
